sections.what: The plugin step that edits the page HTML during the build. It replaces the Open Graph and Twitter image tags with the full image address, and skips the change when no domain or image is found.
sections.why: The top comment states the purpose: correct link previews.
sections.watch_out: The replacement matches exact tag text, so if the tag format changes, the change is silently skipped.

sections.name: getDeploymentUrl
sections.title: Public web address
sections.what: Builds the site's full address from the Replit internal domain variable, and falls back to the dev domain variable. Returns nothing if neither is set.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app is hosted on Replit, which provides these variables.
sections.watch_out: When both variables are set, the internal domain always wins, which may not be what a developer expects.

summary: A build-time add-on that rewrites the social preview image tags in the web page so that link previews show the app's image at the correct web address.
purpose: Makes shared links show the right preview picture on social sites and in chat apps.
why: The top comment says it updates the og:image and twitter:image tags to point to the app's preview image with the correct Replit domain.
how: When the page is built, it picks a web address from the Replit environment variables. It checks for an opengraph image in png, jpg or jpeg form. If it finds one, it replaces the two image tags. Otherwise it leaves the page unchanged.
inputs: The Replit domain environment variables, the image file in the client public folder, and the page HTML.
outputs: A changed HTML page with the image tags updated, or the page unchanged.
risks: Only the two Replit domain variables are supported. If neither is set, the tags are left as they are. The image check uses a path from the current working folder, and it is unclear from these files whether a client/public folder exists in this project. If it does not, the tags are never updated.
debug: Check the two image tags in the built HTML, the Replit domain environment variables, and whether the image exists in the folder the build runs from. Log messages appear only in production builds, so a development run gives no hint when a step is skipped.
